title: Keeper App Project - Part 1 Challenge
summary: Kicks off the section's capstone, the Keeper note-taking app. Part 1 asks for an App component that renders three child components (Header, Note, Footer), styled by matching the classes and element selectors already present in the supplied styles.css.

concepts.heading: Starting project contents
points: index.html is minimal: a <title>, a Google Fonts stylesheet link (McLaren for the logo, Montserrat for body text), a link to styles.css, and the usual empty <div id="root"> that React renders into. (Extra) In the react-scripts starter the bundled index.js is injected automatically; the Vite version in the reference repo loads it explicitly with <script type="module" src="/src/main.jsx">.
styles.css already holds every rule the finished app needs. The job is to write JSX whose element types and class names match those selectors, not to write CSS.
index.js contains the numbered challenge steps as comments.

concepts.heading: Working locally instead of in CodeSandbox
points: Open the starting sandbox from the lecture resources and export it as a zip, then unzip it to get a normal project folder.
Drag the folder into VS Code (add to workspace); older practice folders can be removed from the workspace.
In a terminal, cd into the project folder (e.g. Downloads/keeper-app-part-1) and run npm install. That pulls in react, react-dom and react-scripts as listed in package.json.
Run npm start to launch the dev server and view the app at localhost:3000.
(Extra) Newer Vite-based versions of the starter (as in the reference repo) use npm run dev instead, serve on localhost:5173, and have src/main.jsx as the entry file in place of index.js.

concepts.heading: What the finished Part 1 must contain
points: A new React app with an App component that acts as the root of the tree.
Header component: renders a <header> element with the app name (Keeper, or any name you like) inside an <h1>.

The page should look like the sample finished app linked in the challenge. To get there, read styles.css and work out which classes and which HTML elements each rule targets.

(Extra) In the reference repo styles.css lives in public/ and is linked from index.html with href="/styles.css", so it applies globally without being imported into any component.

task.name: Keeper App Part 1: Header, Note and Footer components
task.starting_point: Starter sandbox (or exported local folder) with index.html, styles.css and an index.js listing the challenge steps as comments. No components exist yet.
task.goal: Build an App component that renders Header, Note and Footer components so the page matches the sample Keeper app: yellow header bar with the app name, one white note card, and a grey copyright footer pinned to the bottom with the current year.
steps: Create the React app entry: in index.js import React and ReactDOM and render into document.getElementById('root').
Create App.jsx exporting an App function component; render <App /> from index.js.
Create Header.jsx that returns a <header> element wrapping an <h1> with the app name.

Create Footer.jsx that returns a
element wrapping a

copyright message; compute the year with new Date().getFullYear() and insert it with curly braces.

Create Note.jsx that returns a
with an

title and a

of content.
Import Header, Note and Footer into App and render them in that order.

Open styles.css, note which selectors target elements (header, header h1, footer, footer p) and which target a class (.note), and add className="note" on the Note component's <div> so the card styling applies.
Compare with the sample app and adjust until it matches; then optionally customise the styles.
task.expected_result: A yellow header strip with white McLaren-font title, a single white rounded card with a bold title and body text floated to the left, and light grey footer text centred at the bottom of the page showing the current year.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.16 Keeper App Project - Part 1 Challenge/keeper-app-part-1-challenge/src

pitfalls: Hard-coding the year in the footer instead of computing it with the Date object.
Wrapping the Footer's text in a plain <div> or the Header's in a <div>: the CSS targets the header and footer elements themselves, so the styles won't apply.
Using class instead of className in JSX for the note card.
Forgetting npm install before npm start when running the exported project locally.
